To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ARG2 is a potential therapeutic target for thyroid cancer.
Arginase 2 is a novel marker of thyroid malignancies.
ARG2 expression is increased in thyroid tumors and that it is involved in the regulation of eNOS, a key enzyme of the nitric oxide synthases (NOS) family.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel role for arginase 2, which has been shown for the first time to be associated with the pathobiology of thyroid tumors.
the role of ARG1 and ARG2 in thyroid tumors, and the potential for targeting these enzymes for cancer therapy.
the identification of new pathways and potential therapeutic strategies for the management of thyroid cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of ARG2 is increased in malignant thyroid tumors and that it plays a role in tumor progression and aggressiveness.
ARG2 is a key regulator of the eNOS pathway and the redox environment in thyroid tumors.
the expression of ARG2 in thyroid tumors is related to the expression of eNOs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ARG2 expression is increased in most malignant tumors, and that ARG2 knockdown decreases tumor properties and nitric oxide production.
ARG2 expression is increased in thyroid cancer cells and its silencing leads to a reduction of eNOS expression and a subsequent reduction in nitric oxide production.
arginase 2 is an important regulator of eNOS expression and activity, which in turn affects tumor properties of thyroid cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of ARG2 in thyroid tumors is associated with increased eNOS and other eNOS-related gene expression and that the underlying mechanism might have major implications for tumor pathogenesis.
ARG2 and NOS may work in concert to promote thyroid tumorigenisis.
the expression levels of the arginase isoforms are not only important to the immune system but also to the development and progression of several cancer types.
